content_voiceover: This slide covers the ICE score, the Immune Effector Cell-associated Encephalopathy assessment tool used to grade CAR-T neurotoxicity, or ICANS. It's a ten-point scale built from five domains. Orientation is worth four points: can the patient state the year, month, city, and hospital. Naming is worth three points: can they name three objects, like a clock, a pen, and a button. Following commands is worth one point, such as holding up two fingers or closing the eyes and sticking out the tongue. Writing a standard sentence is worth one point. And attention, counting backward from one hundred by tens, is worth one point. Four plus three plus one plus one plus one gets you to ten total. The grading cutoffs matter for boards: a score of seven to nine is grade one, three to six is grade two, zero to two is grade three, and if the patient can't be aroused enough to complete the ICE assessment at all, that's automatically grade four, regardless of score. Combine this with seizure activity, elevated intracranial pressure, and motor findings from the full ASTCT ICANS grading system, but the ICE score itself is the piece most likely to be tested directly.
keypoints: ICE score is a 10-point tool: orientation (4), naming (3), commands (1), writing (1), attention (1)
